newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil orders state firms to slash expenses -paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil orders state firms to slash expenses -paper.

text.p: Brazil's federal government has ordered state firms to cut 1.5 billion reais ($1.4 billion) in expenses in 1997, local newspapers said on Thursday.
Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper said the cuts would allow for a primary budget surplus of 7.0 billion reais or 0.85 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year.
The government aims to reach a public sector primary surplus of 1.5 percent of GDP in 1997.
Petrobras, Eletrobras and Telebras are the state companies that will suffer the biggest cuts in their budgets, Folha said.
Petrobras will have to cut 776 million reais, Eletrobras must reduce 195 million reais, while Telebras will have to show a 269 million reais cut in expenses, it added.
((--Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 2485412)) ($ = 1.069 Brazilian Reais)
